mission: 'An AI safety research group at Mila led by David Krueger.' The lab began at the University of Cambridge (it ran an ERA–KASL internship there in 2024) and moved with Krueger to Mila / Université de Montréal. It studies reward gaming, goal misgeneralisation, scaling and foundational challenges of LLM alignment; Krueger is also a prominent public advocate for slowing frontier AI. Founding year approximate. (Site's TLS certificate was expired when visited.)

key_work.title: Foundational Challenges in Assuring Alignment and Safety of Large Language Models
key_work.plain_summary: With 35+ co-authors, identifies 18 foundational challenges and 200+ open research questions for making LLMs safe.

key_work.title: Goal Misgeneralization in Deep Reinforcement Learning
key_work.plain_summary: Shows agents can competently pursue the wrong goal in new situations even when trained with the right reward.

key_work.title: Defining and Characterizing Reward Gaming
key_work.plain_summary: Gives a formal definition of when optimising a proxy reward is 'hackable' and shows unhackable proxies are very rare.

key_work.title: Broken Neural Scaling Laws
key_work.plain_summary: A functional form that better predicts how AI performance changes with scale, including sudden jumps.

people.role: Lab lead; assistant professor, Université de Montréal / Mila

warnings.text: Models can pursue unintended goals competently when circumstances change (goal misgeneralisation).
Almost any proxy reward can be 'gamed' by a strong enough optimiser (reward gaming).
Krueger publicly warns of human extinction risk and has urged governments to bring frontier development to a halt (2026 interviews).

recommendations.text: Prioritise the 18 foundational challenges in LLM assurance as a research agenda.
Governments should be ready to stop or pause dangerous frontier AI development (Krueger's advocacy).
